subject: Silverpine private-connect cutover — intermittent large-packet failures and NAT port saturation
messages:
From: Anna Voss <anna.voss@silverpine.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@silverpine.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 23:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-cutover: large uploads intermittently fail (Silverpine private connect)

Hi Irene,

We completed the private-connect cutover to Redwood last night (cutover window 02:00-03:00 local). Since then our customers have reported intermittent failures uploading large artifacts (20MB+). Our application logs show repeated TCP retransmits and a subset of flows that never complete.

What we've observed so far:
- Failures are more frequent on large packets (MTU-related?), small payloads are fine.
- Our on-prem firewall logs show MSS clamping at 1460 occasionally and some "fragmentation needed" ICMPs dropped by a middlebox.
- We see many short-lived NAT entries and ephemeral port exhaustion spikes around the same timeframe.

I attached a tcpdump captured at our gateway during a failed upload attempt and a copy of the gateway config before/after the cutover. Can someone triage urgently — this is impacting uploads for paying customers.

Attachments: silverpine_tcpdump_20270425.pcap (pcap, ~2.1MB); silverpine_gateway_config_before_after.txt (text)

Thanks,
Anna Voss
Head of Infrastructure
Silverpine Systems

Subject: Re: Post-cutover: large uploads intermittently fail (Silverpine private connect)

Anna — thanks for the clear notes and the pcap. We’ve escalated this to our network triage and private-deploy teams and will treat this as a high-priority incident.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Karthik — can you review the pcap and gateway config for MTU/MSS/fragmentation symptoms and NAT session counts?
2) Marissa — please prepare a short rollback and a minimal remediation play to run during a narrow maintenance window.
3) Vanessa — can you check our VPC egress SNAT pool sizing and whether there were any rapid port allocation spikes on the Redwood side during the cutover?

Anna — would you be able to confirm a 60-minute window today (preferably 09:00-10:00 PDT) for us to run active tests and a transient MSS clamp on the Silverpine gateway? We’ll coordinate a clear rollback if anything degrades.

I’ll keep you posted with findings in this thread.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Anna Voss <anna.voss@silverpine.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: large uploads intermittently fail (Silverpine private connect)

Quick triage notes after reviewing the pcap and configs attached:
- The tcpdump shows clear signs of PMTU blackholing: SYN/ACKs succeed then larger segments (1460-1500) trigger retransmits and we observe ICMP "fragmentation needed" that are either not passed back to the sender or are rate-limited.
- The Silverpine gateway NAT config shows a relatively small SNAT pool (1024 ports per public IP) and an aggressive connection timeout for ephemeral mappings. During the cutover we can see many short connections which looks like port churn + rapid allocation.
- I also see the on-prem firewall doing MSS clamping inconsistently — some sessions are clamped to 1400, some to 1460. That mismatch explains why only a subset of flows fail (the ones not clamped hit the blackhole).

Suggested immediate mitigations to test in the window Anna proposed:
1) Apply forced MSS clamp to 1400 on the Silverpine gateway egress (temporary, reversible).
   - Example iptables/iproute snippet (attach): --/-m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400
2) Increase SNAT ephemeral port pool on the gateway / allocate an extra public IP for SNAT overflow during the cutover.
3) On Redwood side, temporarily extend NAT timeout and enable prefix caching to reduce churn (we can do this from our control plane).
4) Run active file upload tests (varying MSS) and collect simultaneous tcpdumps from both sides and our egress node.

I’ve attached a short triage-playbook.md with commands and rollback steps. If MSS clamp fixes repros, we can investigate why middlebox ICMPs are not getting through and work on a long-term fix (MTU alignment across cutover path).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: triage-playbook.md (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Anna Voss <anna.voss@silverpine.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: large uploads intermittently fail (Silverpine private connect)

Action plan for 09:00-10:00 PDT window today (summary & checklist):
- 09:00: Prepare on-call runbook and notify CS/Support; take baseline metrics.
- 09:05: Apply MSS clamp 1400 on Silverpine gateway (ops to apply).
- 09:10: Allocate an additional public IP on Silverpine SNAT pool and temporarily increase ephemeral port pool.
- 09:15: Redwood: extend NAT idle timeout to 300s and enable prefix caching for Silverpine route.
- 09:20-09:40: Run three concurrent upload tests with client and server tcpdumps (we’ll capture both ends).
- 09:45: If success >95% for uploads, revert MSS clamp to 1460 for 5-minute observation, then plan long-term alignment. If failures continue, rollback immediately and open deeper packet-trace loop.

Rollback: Remove added public IP and revert NAT timeouts + MSS clamp. Post-run: collect all tcpdumps and a sample of conntrack state snapshots (we’ll attach).

I’ll own orchestration and rollback. Vanessa — please confirm if Redwood can change NAT timeout and prefix caching for this tenant now (we have elevated ops access for the cutover).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
